visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) [People: Face/Hands] A man in a black t-shirt sits on a pallet bench, looking slightly annoyed. A woman in a beige t-shirt enters from the right, handing him a McDonald's cup. [Objects: Details/State] Two McFlurry cups with visible brownie chunks on top. [Setting: Background/Lighting] Bright outdoor urban square with red-walled buildings and a B1 sign. (2) [People: Face/Hands] The woman points at the cup, explaining her layered eating method. The man makes gestures of disagreement, scratching his ear and frowning. [Objects: Details/State] Close-up of the McFlurry showing dark chocolate powder and brownies. [Setting: Background/Lighting] Same outdoor setting, natural bright daylight reflecting off the buildings. (3) [People: Face/Hands] The man vigorously stirs his McFlurry with a spoon, demonstrating his mixed method. Animated text graphics like braised pork rice appear to illustrate his point. [Objects: Details/State] The McFlurry changes from a layered look to a uniform brown mixture. [Setting: Background/Lighting] Outdoor square, street level view with some trees in the background. (4) [People: Face/Hands] The woman takes a bite, her face showing pure delight with a big smile. She points her finger to emphasize the taste. The man eats his mixed version with a satisfied nod. [Objects: Details/State] Spoons and half-eaten dessert cups are held in their hands. [Setting: Background/Lighting] Background includes some blurred pedestrians walking by. (5) [People: Face/Hands] Both characters face the camera, holding their cups high and smiling widely. They speak the promotional slogan together with animated gestures. [Objects: Details/State] Large yellow and white text overlays appear on screen for the finale. [Setting: Background/Lighting] Final shot in the same urban park area under natural light.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to promote McDonald's new Cocoa Brownie McFlurry by using a humorous debate between two creators about the best way to eat it—layered versus mixed—while highlighting the product's textures and ingredients.
